extraction.Name: Joseph Weber
extraction.Refused/Protested: while he did not make application for the patent in fee to his 160 acre allotment when it was issued, April 13, 1918, he was perfectly willing to accept it when it was sent to him; and that he has never regretted it
extraction.Buyer: in 1923, jointly mortgaged his 160 acre allotment with his brother, Frank, sister, Julia, and his mother, Emma Weber, latter having 632.16 acres, to the Federal Land Association, of Omaha, Nebraska, for the sum of $7000.00; in 1927, sold his allotment to his father, William Weber, who took over the responsibility of the mortgage against the land, and paying deponent the sum of $480.00 over and above the mortgage against it
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: he has kept the taxes paid up on his allotment all these years; he did not sell his land for any debts made prior to receiving the patent in fee
extraction.Occupation/Income: he is a barber; and that his trade is his only income
extraction.NOTES: mentally competent; health is good; married, having his wife only to support; wife has good health; mortgage was obtained to buy three sections of land purchased in the name of the father William Weber; allotment described as being in the sand hills; has never received any aid from the County, State nor the United States Government; affidavit sworn April 2, 1929 | ORIGINAL_TRIBE_VALUE: "Pine Ridge (Shannon County, South Dakota)" (normalized 2026-04-28 to canonical 'Pine Ridge')

recovery_notes.rationale: Pine Ridge tribe field had 40+ string variants across the corpus. Consolidating to canonical 'Pine Ridge' for clean tabulation while preserving original variant in NOTES for audit.
